newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Vodacom buys 25 pct of Cellphones Direct.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Vodacom buys 25 pct of Cellphones Direct.

text.p: South African mobile phone network firm Vodacom said on Friday it had bought a 25 percent stake in service provider Cellphones Direct in a "multi-million rand" deal.
No actual price tag was given for the purchase.

"We have always recognised distribution as one of the key factors in our growth and as the only direct response service provider in the market, Cellphones Direct gives Vodacom another route to the market," Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig said in a statement.
Vodacom shareholder, Vodafone Group Plc, holds a 16 percent stake in Cellphones Direct's parent, a U.K.-based firm of the same name. Vodafone holds a 31.5 percent stake in Vodacom.

Mervyn Visagie, managing director of Cellphones Direct, said plans were in progress to diversify the company's product range into "synergy niches" including other telecommunications and information technology products or services.
